title.purpose: Doubled body atlas for location and modal headings.

body.purpose: Native menu copy, destinations and actions.

label.purpose: Compact metadata, footer commands and notifications.

components.name: Framed modal
components.description: Native layered frame from LagoonUI_Frame. HTML/CSS is a documentation translation; the game draws clipped rectangles.

components.name: Selected action
components.description: Tonal band and drawn gold cursor. Browser hover/focus previews native selection; the game itself has no pointer-hover state.

components.name: Options tabs
components.description: Five fixed native tabs; gold text and a two-pixel underline identify the active tab. Preview states translate shoulder/key selection.

components.name: Volume and progress
components.description: Shared gray track and gold fill from settings/achievement code. This sample documents a readout, not a new mouse slider.

components.name: Travel confirmation
components.description: A second shared frame separates a deliberate return confirmation from the availability view; no gameplay action is implied by this static preview.

narrative.overview:
The original game's black dialogue windows and light frames establish the visual
authority. The native map, Options and achievement browser extend that world with
readable sentence-case lettering, restrained gold selection and persistent control
hints. Original scenery supplies the imagery; the interface supplies orientation.

These are controller and keyboard surfaces drawn by C into authored pixel canvases.
Their text is independent of mutable game glyphs and the optional gameplay EPX
pass. The system favors a clear selected action over decorative motion or depth.
keyCharacteristics: Black fields with layered ivory frames.
Proportional lowercase lettering and a small, explicit type ramp.
Gold cursors, active tabs and progress; quiet secondary information.
Finite original terrain with fixed-size map labels and landmarks.
Visible keyboard/controller commands at the bottom of each modal.

rules.name: The Selection Rule
rules.body: Gold identifies the active choice, meaningful progress or a map landmark. Ordinary paragraph text remains ivory or quiet gray.

rules.name: The Fixed Label Rule
rules.body: Terrain zoom changes terrain and landmark positions; map headings, labels and command hints keep their authored size.

rules.name: The Frame Rule
rules.body: Use the shared layered frame to establish a modal or bounded map region; use a thin divider to separate content within it.

dos: **Do** use the shared frame and immutable menu font for new host panels.
**Do** keep map labels fixed while terrain pans or zooms.
**Do** expose selection and keyboard/controller commands without relying on color alone.
**Do** distinguish current scenery, a last mapped visit and unavailable scenery honestly.
**Do** use actual progress and read-only reference data for journal and item copy.
donts: **Don't** apply gameplay EPX or mutable game-glyph uploads to opaque host-menu text.
**Don't** use viewing or navigation as an implicit confirmation of a gameplay action.
**Don't** replace original scenery with decorative illustrations or a whole-game retexture.
**Don't** treat a discovered exit landmark as proof that its story gate is unlocked.
